title: 0.5 M EDTA (0.5 L) Preparation
author: Mattia Pegoraro
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xr2fm8e

steps.title: Prepare water in container
steps.instruction: Fill a 0.5 L beaker with 300 mL deionized water.

steps.title: Add EDTA disodium salt
steps.instruction: Add 73.06 g (molar mass 292.24 g mol⁻¹) of EDTA disodium salt to the water and mix until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Adjust pH to 8
steps.instruction: Add NaOH pellets while stirring until the pH reaches ~7.8 (solution becomes clear around pH 7.5); then fine‑tune to pH 8 using 5 M NaOH (10 M NaOH may also be used).

substeps.instruction: Add NaOH pellets until pH ≈7.8 (solution clears near pH 7.5).
Add 5 M NaOH dropwise (or 10 M NaOH) to reach pH 8.

steps.title: Bring volume to final 500 mL
steps.instruction: After pH adjustment, add deionized water to bring the total volume to 500 mL, yielding a 0.5 M EDTA solution in 0.5 L.

steps.title: Sterilize solution
steps.instruction: Sterilize the solution by autoclaving at 121 °C for 15 min (00:15:00) or by filtration through a 0.22 µm filter.

steps.title: Verify final pH
steps.instruction: Insert a pH electrode into the solution with continuous mixing and measure the pH; the solution may appear cloudy and initially read ~3, but the target pH is 8.
